text:
jordan.l: hi all, first week here — trying to access Console -> Staging -> Feature Flags and getting a 403. can anyone point me to who sets those permissions?
tanya.m: welcome Jordan! :tada: usually infra-ops handles group assignments for flags. did you sign in via SSO and accept the org invite?
jordan.l: yep accepted SSO invite. can view the main console and service list but when I click Flags it shows: `403 Forbidden` and small message "You do not have permission to view this page. Contact your admin."
sam.k: that sounds like a missing role. we gate staging flags behind the `flags-staging-access` group. @infra-ops can you check if jordan.l is provisioned properly?
infra-ops: on it. please DM me the exact email you used to sign in.
jordan.l: jordan.l@redwood.ai
infra-ops: thanks. i'm seeing a partial SSO provision (user created but without group sync). i'll trigger a SCIM sync and add the user to flags-staging-access. give me ~3 minutes.
console-bot: FYI: when roles change you'll see an audit entry under Console > Admin > Audit Logs. Docs: https://console.redwood.internal/admin/audit
tanya.m: if you're blocked, I can run a quick preview of the staging flags for you (read-only) — `GET /internal/flags/preview?env=staging&user=jordan.l` and paste the JSON. LMK.
infra-ops: sync complete and user was added to flags-staging-access at 1800123468. try a hard refresh or open an incognito window.
jordan.l: still 403 in the same browser. incognito fixed it — I can see the flags list but toggles are disabled (read-only). is that expected?
sam.k: yes, by default we give read-only to new engineers for staging flags; write toggles require the `flags-staging-operators` role which is granted on request after a short onboarding checklist.
jordan.l: what's the checklist? I might need toggle access for a debugging session.
tanya.m: checklist: 1) quick flags walkthrough with your tech lead, 2) confirm you've read the rollback playbook (link in handbook), 3) permission request in the access repo with approver CC'd. usually takes <24h.
jordan.l: okay i'll do that. one last q: if I flip a flag in staging, does that trigger model reloads or any heavy infra ops? don't want to accidentally cause load.
sam.k: most flags are logical switches and don't require a model reload. exceptions are ones that change batching/quantization profiles — those will warm caches and may cause higher GPU memory/shutdown churn. such flags are prefixed `infra/batch/` and require an ops-notify.
jordan.l: good to know. thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help! :pray:
console-bot: Access change: user jordan.l was added to group flags-staging-access by infra-ops at 1800123468.
